# RV2-D pre-registration (generated by freeze_prereg.py; written before any confirmatory seed ran)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-routing-v2-stage4-design.md` (sections 4 to 9 and 13) with the amendments of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-routing-v2-stage4-AMENDMENTS.md` (A4-1 changes the denominator of S4-5; A4-2 the pool seed of the function-regime streams). Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-15-routing-v2-stage4.md`. Build record: notebook E-033; dev runs (code stamp e468a8911472d079): `RESULTS_DEV_REVIEW.md`, `DEV_SELECTION.md`. Confirmatory seeds 85-99 (single use): the ten stage-3 streams 15 seeds, arithmetic operator-by-operator 85-90, banking77 85-89, arithmetic mixed from 16 and from 128 units 15 seeds. Dev seeds are 100 and above.

## Arms

`S3` = the stage-3 pool as it stands (batch-level gate on, breaker 12 / 0.5 / 100, persistence 2, group veto 0.2; the budget tuned for A_vote); `S3+T` adds `spawn_rule="transfer"`; `S3+G` adds `growth_rule="gap"`; `S3+T+G` both. The router (`router=True`) is evaluated on the SAME trained pools of every arm (it acts at answer time only and never influences training), so router off and on are paired by construction. Arithmetic: hidden 512, replay 20,000, 5 inner steps (mixed streams: hidden 16 or 128). The function-regime streams use the pool seed `stream seed + 7` (A4-2); arithmetic and banking77 keep the stream seed.

## Constants (chosen on dev seeds by the declared rules; the curves are in `DEV_SELECTION.md`)

- `grow_gap` = 0.17 (rule: spec 6.7, score = accuracy gain minus 0.1 x relative parameter increase over three groups, subject to the guards of S4-7); `grow_guard_eps` = 0.02, `grow_guard_window` = 100
- `transfer_margin` = 0.25 (rule: best arithmetic gain among the margins that keep the guard streams within -0.5 points and 1.2 x the experts; ties to 0.25), `transfer_alpha` = 0.01
- router: mode `free`, margin 0.01 (rule: best mean gain on arithmetic and OV-0.85 among the settings that hurt no guard stream by more than 0.5 points)
- overrides applied (each with its reason in `constants_override.json`): none
- `bars_rv2d.json` sha256 f445f86018dc1034; code stamp ff3438232c5f0dfa

## Decision rules (verbatim from the spec, section 8)

Each component is adopted on its own: 4a if S4-1 or S4-2 and S4-3 pass; 4b if S4-4 and S4-5 pass; 4c if S4-6 and S4-7 pass; adopting means the default flips, the old entry points are pinned in the experiment scripts, and notes go wherever the old behaviour was documented. Kill rules: if a guard fails the component stays OFF and the others proceed; if the router's selection picks a worse rule than density on any guard stream by more than 0.5 points the margin is raised to 0.03 and the guard rerun once; the stage-3 statements S3-1 to S3-9 must still pass with every adopted component (golden and the stage-3 tests). S4-9 failing is a bug, not a result: stop. S4-8 (the full stack) flags the adoption when it misses.

## Reported, not gated

CPU seconds per arm; experts, spawns and extends per stream; growth events, reverts and widths per run; the router rule selected per stream and its cross-validated accuracies; the cost of the extra forward pass of the growth rule; the merge audit (E-033, F-28); a transfer-rule diagnostic on the one-function arithmetic stream (dev only).

## What is claimed, and what is not

Only what the tested streams show: the router's gain is a property of operator-like and heavily overlapping regimes; the growth threshold is an operating point; the transfer rule cannot rely on merge to clean up false spawns (a wrongly founded expert is permanent), which is why the expert counts are gated (S4-5). Nothing here concerns streams, widths or budgets that were not run.
